explain.say: A beam bridge is the simplest bridge: a stiff beam resting on supports at each end. A truck on top pushes down with its weight.

explain.say: The beam must also carry its own weight, which for a concrete or steel deck is a lot. Under all that load the beam bends a little, its top squashed and its bottom stretched.

forces.label: Deck's own weight
forces.ask: Why do beam bridges have short spans?

explain.say: The piers and abutments push back up with the same total force, so the bridge stays still. The beam's job is to carry the load sideways across the gap to them.

forces.ask: Why does a beam bend in the middle?

forces.label: Deck's own weight
forces.ask: Why do beam bridges have short spans?

explain.say: Double the span and the bending in the middle grows about four times, because there is more load and it acts farther from the supports. That is why beam bridges use many short spans, or deep box girders for longer ones.

faq.q: How does a beam bridge work?
faq.a: A stiff beam rests on supports and carries loads sideways across the gap. The beam bends slightly, and the supports push up to hold the weight.

faq.q: Why does a beam bend in the middle?
faq.a: The load pushes down between the supports, so the beam sags most where it is farthest from them. Its top edge is squashed and its bottom edge stretched.
asks: Where does a beam bend most?

faq.q: Why do beam bridges have short spans?
faq.a: Bending grows with the square of the span, and a longer beam is heavier too. Past a certain length the beam spends most of its strength holding itself up, so long crossings use many piers.
asks: How long can a beam bridge be?
Why do beam bridges need lots of piers?

faq.a: Piers are the supports in the middle of a bridge, and abutments are the ones at each end. They push up on the beam and carry the load down to the foundations.
A box girder is a hollow beam shaped like a long box. Putting material at the top and bottom, far from the middle, makes it very stiff for its weight, so it can span farther.

facts: For an evenly loaded beam, the bending in the middle grows with the square of the span, so doubling the span roughly quadruples it.
The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in Louisiana, about 38 kilometres long, is built from many short concrete beam spans on piles.

quiz.say: If you double the span of a simple beam bridge with the same load on each metre, the bending in the middle grows by about how much?
quiz.show: Double the span: bending grows about…
quiz.why: For an even load, the bending in the middle depends on the span squared, so doubling the span makes it about four times bigger.

wrong.0: There is twice as much load, but it also acts twice as far from the supports, so the effect is more than double.
wrong.2: A longer beam always bends more under the same load per metre.
